label: Look — moody atmospheric (subtractive palette, split grade)
brief: Editorial Pacific-Northwest mood: low-key, quiet, rolled-off highlights, colour by subtraction. Teal/slate shadows against amber/gold highlights; foliage tamed toward olive, skies toward slate. Colour intensity comes only from grading and selective HSL, never from global Saturation. Limits (keep within them on every pass): Saturation -15..0, never positive; Vibrance +5..+20; Contrast at most +10 (no tone curve yet, so build depth with Blacks, Highlights and masks, not Contrast); Clarity -10..+5, never crunchy; no harsh digital whites. Tones (luma 0-255): deep but not crushed floor, p1/p5 about 15-25; low-key middle, p50 about 80-100; highlight ceiling held down, p95 about 185-200 and p99 under about 215. Masks, in this order when the scene allows: (1) vignette: radial over the focal point, inverted: exposure -0.45, highlights -35, dehaze +8, saturation -15. (2) Atmospheric light bleed: radial at the light source or horizon gap: exposure +0.35, temperature +12 (warm), dehaze -15, texture -20, clarity -15 (a soft bloom, not haze over the whole frame). (3) Foreground anchor: linear from the bottom: exposure -0.30, shadows -15, clarity +10. Pass 0 sets the hues of the palette; the variant sets its strength (A subtle, B full, C bold). Keep the palette's hues; refine amounts. The user's own request wins wherever it disagrees with this look.
convergence_hints: stop when p50 sits about 80-100 and p99 under about 215 with no high clip: low-key, highlights rolled off
stop when shadows read teal/slate and highlights amber, and foliage is olive, not bright green
never raise global Saturation or push Clarity past +5 to add punch: use grading, HSL or a mask
